summary: Prototype security rules enforce read-only access on the public model catalog and strict create-only schema/length/timestamp/90-day-TTL validation on AI content reports, paired with Firebase App Check (Play Integrity in release, Debug provider in debug). All client reads, updates, and deletes on reports and unknown collections are denied.

findings.issue: App reports do not require user sign-in (to allow frictionless safety reporting), so rules rely on Firebase App Check (Play Integrity) enforcement at the Firestore service layer plus strict field/size/timestamp validation in rules.
findings.recommendation: Register the release Play Integrity SHA-256 certificate in Firebase Console > App Check and enable App Check enforcement for Cloud Firestore once tested.

findings.issue: Client report reads, updates, and deletes are strictly denied (`allow read, update, delete: if false;`), preventing the Update Bypass and PII leaks. Administrator review uses IAM-authenticated console/admin access.

Every created report must include an `expiresAt` timestamp strictly between 89 and 91 days after `request.time`. Server-side automatic deletion requires the Firestore TTL policy on `ai_content_reports.expiresAt` to be active in Google Cloud / Firebase.
findings.recommendation: Ensure the Firestore TTL policy on collection group `ai_content_reports` field `expiresAt` is enabled in Google Cloud.
